turns.doctor_question: Did all of this start after something particularly stressful happened in your life?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I guess you could trace it back to when the clinic completely overhauled the electronic medical records system and changed up the whole workflow. That messed with my hours pretty badly. It's been almost two years since that happened, if you can believe it. Two years. 

And man, that new EMR system... it's a nightmare. They brought in these consultants, right? These guys in sharp suits who probably haven't stepped foot in a clinic since they got their flu shots. They kept talking about "synergy" and "optimizing patient throughput." One of them, I think his name was Chad, he kept using the word "bandwidth" to talk about human beings. Like we're routers or something. Anyway, they switched us from this older system—which, sure, was a little clunky, but we all knew how to use it—to this shiny new one that crashes if you look at it wrong. 

I remember the first week we went live with it, the whole network went down for three hours. Three hours! We had patients sitting in the waiting room getting more and more agitated. Mrs. Gable, she's this sweet lady who comes in for her blood pressure checks, she brought us a tin of homemade snickerdoodles that day. She always brings cookies. Her husband used to be a baker before he passed away. He made the best pumpernickel bread in the Bronx. But yeah, we were all just sitting there eating snickerdoodles while the IT guys ran around sweating through their polo shirts. So, yeah, the stress from all that change and my hours getting shifted around... that's when this whole heavy feeling really started settling in, about two years ago.
